runner_classes.ubuntu-24.04: SPEC §9 limits on hosted x64 Linux, without host-specific slack.
runner_classes.ubuntu-24.04-arm: Same limits on hosted arm64 Linux; architecture is not grounds for widening.
runner_classes.macos-14: SPEC §9 M-series reference class; the limits apply directly.
runner_classes.macos-15-intel: Same limits on hosted x64 macOS; architecture is not grounds for widening.
runner_classes.windows-latest: Same limits on hosted x64 Windows, including process startup.
runner_classes.windows-11-arm: Same limits on hosted arm64 Windows, including process startup.

reasons.latency_scope: Every latency limit below is the SPEC §9 number, applied unscaled on every synthetic workload. Per-call cost is dominated by process start, database open and bounded top-k work rather than corpus size, so a smaller corpus gets no smaller limit, and passing on a small corpus is not evidence for the full history, which is measured separately on the owner's history. The 2M-row dense workload carries the 2x headroom SPEC §9 requires of 2M-row workloads on hosted runners. Every dense-workload latency applies a factor of 0.5 to its ordinary limit, for both median and p95; first_index uses dense_index_ms and the written size factor. All other warm cases gate both median and p95 against their published limit; every first-index sample must pass.
reasons.keyword_p50_ms: SPEC §9 warm keyword p50 <=40 ms; all search shapes, including counts and compact rendering, finish the full process.
reasons.keyword_p95_ms: SPEC §9 warm keyword p95 <=80 ms; 20 samples minimum, none discarded.
reasons.recall_ms: SPEC §9 recall <=250 ms warm; pack shares its retrieval/window budget.
reasons.census_ms: SPEC §9 no-change census <=15 ms, measured conservatively through full index command exit.
reasons.incremental_ms: SPEC §9 one-session incremental refresh <=50 ms through full index command exit.
reasons.first_index_ms: SPEC §9 first full index of the owner's history (reference_rows visible rows, reference_text_bytes of indexed text) <=60 s. A synthetic workload gets 60000 x min(1, max(rows / reference_rows, text_bytes / reference_text_bytes)): with build cost linear in rows and indexed text, that is the longest an engine meeting the full-history target could take on it. Example: 100000 rows with 88600000 text bytes gives 60000 x 0.1 = 6000 ms. The 1000-row semantic workload has no build limit: fixed per-build costs dominate at that size, and builds are gated by the mixed and dense workloads.
reasons.dense_index_ms: The first_index_ms derivation with the 2x headroom SPEC §9 requires of 2M-row workloads: 30000 x the same factor, which is 1 because 2M rows exceed reference_rows.
reasons.dense_p50_ms: SPEC §9 requires 2x headroom for 2M scale workloads: half the 40 ms keyword p50 deadline.
reasons.dense_p95_ms: SPEC §9 requires 2x headroom for 2M scale workloads: half the 80 ms keyword p95 deadline.
reasons.hybrid_p50_ms: SPEC §9 warm agent hybrid p50 <=200 ms, with a labeled semantic row required. The CI semantic workload holds 1000 vectors, so this limit covers model load, query embedding, keyword retrieval, fusion and rendering; vector-scan cost at owner scale is measured on the 200000-reference semantic workload.
reasons.hybrid_first_ms: SPEC §9 first hybrid query with the model installed <=1 s: a fresh CLI process after model installation and corpus embedding, with meaning results required.
reasons.reference_rows: Visible rows in the owner's full-history build: 130469 prose + 1071908 tool rows.
reasons.reference_text_bytes: Indexed text in the owner's history: about 820 MB of tool text plus 66 MB of prose.
